items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] Can an African feminist have a white wedding? It’s complicated | Patience Akumu
items.content_html:
I wanted to be a beacon of black feminist love; my friends and family teased me for being a sellout

We had been together 20 years, had two children and had a customary marriage with our village sub-county two years ago without any real plans for a church wedding. So we called our second ceremony a celebration of love and not a wedding. How else would a self-professed African feminist survive being the centre of a colonial and Abrahamic religious ceremony that also manages to reinforce the most male-centred aspects of African culture?

Our invitations came directly from me and my partner Mark, not – as is traditional – from our families, and in the form of a playful gif featuring the song Love Potion from the South African group Mafikizolo, a reminder that this was a wedding on our terms. I thought they screamed “liberated African feminist”. But when my cousin Moses received his, he asked, “So, the patriarchy has won?”

Continue reading...

items.title: [firstpost.com] Israeli opposition backs Eisenkot as Arab parties hold balance of power
items.content_html: Israeli opposition leaders are meeting Tuesday to coordinate support for former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government after an October 27 election left no bloc with a majority. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp won 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while Jewish-led opposition parties won 48. Arab-majority parties won 19, making their support potentially decisive. The opposition’s central dispute is whether to rely on Arab lawmakers. Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats, supports cooperation, while Avigdor Lieberman of Yisrael Beiteinu opposes an Arab-backed minority government. Lieberman has nevertheless said his party will recommend Eisenkot. Netanyahu is calling for a broad government under his leadership that excludes Arab parties, which he accuses of supporting terrorism and rejecting Israel’s Jewish character. President Isaac Herzog is due to receive the certified results and begin party consultations on November 4, then choose a lawmaker by November 11 to try to form a government. The nominee has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. If coalition efforts fail, further parliamentary steps could lead to a new election.

items.title: [aljazeera.com] Six-day Ukraine-Russia truce ends as emergency apps are hacked
items.content_html: A six-day ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in Ukraine’s Kherson region ended late Nov. 1 after Moscow declined Kyiv’s offer to extend it, Ukrainian officials said. The pause, brokered with help from U.S. first lady Melania Trump and with the involvement of Pope Leo XIV, enabled humanitarian deliveries and evacuations. Neither side reported violations during the truce. Within hours of the truce’s end, Ukraine said its nationwide air-raid alert app had been compromised and briefly sent false warnings of radiation, nuclear and chemical threats, street fighting and Russia’s Oreshnik missile. Ukraine’s Air Force said there was no radiation threat, and the Ukrainian strategic communications center blamed Russia for the hack. Russia later said its emergencies app had suffered a “massive cyberattack” that spread false information but did not identify a perpetrator. It was unclear whether the two incidents were connected. Fighting continued elsewhere: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian attacks had left hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian households without power. He offered to stop Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries if Washington supplied Patriot interceptor missiles. U.S.-mediated talks are expected to resume in November after stalling following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

items.title: [theguardian.com] France protests draw 320,000 as clashes spread to German cities
items.content_html: About 320,000 people protested across France on Saturday, Oct. 31, in a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over living costs, education and public services; youth groups put turnout closer to 500,000. Most marches were peaceful, but clashes broke out as crowds dispersed in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and Toulouse. Police used tear gas, water cannon and baton charges, and authorities reported more than 560 arrests nationwide. A Molotov cocktail struck a police officer in Paris in what Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called attempted murder. The movement began with students protesting poor school conditions, teacher shortages and university admissions they say disadvantage poorer applicants, then drew unions and Yellow Vest activists. The government’s turnout estimate fell from 410,000 the previous weekend and 550,000 on Oct. 17, when riots and looting damaged shops and public buildings. Student organizations have called for school and university blockades, while a general strike is expected in the coming days. The GenZ regelt! campaign also organized youth-led protests in 34 German cities over living costs, education funding and compulsory military service. After largely peaceful daytime marches, violence erupted in Frankfurt, where shops were looted and a gun store was among those targeted. Police said they arrested a suspect and seized two weapons. Police also used water cannon or pepper spray in several cities.

items.title: [AI Feed Curator] State of the Feed — Week of October 26–1, 2026
items.content_html:
Over the week of October 26 to November 1, 2026, the aggregator completed 7 runs, fetching an average of 1,471 articles per run and delivering an average of 83 quality-passing articles per run. Category volume was led by ai-tech (126 articles), followed by news (101), climate (73), wellness (70), science (57), design (42), homelab (38), local (45), homestead (15), outdoors (9), and scifi (8). Articles were scored on the dimensional Q/R/L composite (quality, relevance, local) with weights of 0.25, 0.55, and 0.20 respectively. Across the 14 runs measured to date, the mean noise-to-signal ratio was 2.27 articles fetched per article delivered, within a range of 0.88 to 3.16, indicating that pipeline filtering remained moderate and did not show a notably high or low ratio this week.

Feed maintenance this week included the addition of 14 new feeds: BOOKSTEVE'S LIBRARY, Guy Kawasaki, PsyBlog, Psychology Headlines Around the World, MIT News - Artificial intelligence, Climate Crisis – Brave New Europe, The Province, Tŝilhqot'in National Government, Bambu Lab Community Forum - Latest posts, 3D Printing Industry, Dreaming3D Inc - News, and two entries for Radio Circuits Blog. One feed, Hacker News, reported errors during the period and requires attention. Feed discovery surfaced three leading candidates: ABC News (score 82.3), AI as Normal Technology (score 76.7), and a second ABC News entry (score 76.4).
